statement.text: Let $\alpha,\beta\in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that $\alpha/\beta$ is irrational. Is the multiset $ \{ \lfloor \alpha\rfloor,\lfloor 2\alpha\rfloor,\lfloor 4\alpha\rfloor,\ldots\}\cup \{ \lfloor \beta\rfloor,\lfloor 2\beta\rfloor,\lfloor 4\beta\rfloor,\ldots\} $ complete? That is, can all sufficiently large natural numbers $n$ be written as $ n=\sum_{s\in S}\lfloor 2^s\alpha\rfloor+\sum_{t\in T}\lfloor 2^t\beta\rfloor $ for some finite $S,T\subset \mathbb{N}$? What if $2$ is replaced by some $\gamma\in(1,2)$?

title: Erdős Problem #354
